newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss stocks end lower as blue chips lose momentum.
newsitem.headline: Swiss stocks end lower as blue chips lose momentum.

text.p: Swiss shares failed to maintain an early upward drive, snapping a four-day bull run to end lower on Wednesday as bourse heavyweights such as Novartis, UBS and Nestle turned negative on early Wall Street losses.
The market focused on insurer Winterthur, whose extreme volatility was representative of the whole market, dealers said.
Winterthur shares gave up most of their eight percent gain but still closed 16 Swiss francs higher at 1,420 after the company said its share price was excessive.
The blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI) shed 35.5 points, or 0.59 percent, to 5,977.1.
The SMI had touched an all-time high at 6,101.2 points in early trade, powering ahead after breaching the psychologically important level of 6,000 points on Tuesday.
The all-share Swiss Performance Index (SPI) slipped 15.62 points, or 0.41 percent, to 3,753.17.
Bourse volume reached a hefty 3.69 billion Swiss francs.

Unconfirmed rumours have circulated in the market that Winterthur could be subject of a takeover bid or may reinforce its ties with bank group Credit Suisse Group, but dealers said this speculation was old.
A Winterthur spokeswoman said the firm did not plan any kind of substantial changes.
Credit Suisse Group lost two francs to 207.25. UBS bearers slid 11 francs to 1,729.

Shares of technology group Sulzer were among the star performers. Dealers said this stemmed from the fact that its Sulzer Medica unit said sales in the first six months of 1997 rose 22 percent to 704 million Swiss francs.
Sulzer Medica is in the process of being partially spun off. Trade in Sulzer Medica will start next week.
Among pharmaceutical shares, Novartis registereds fell 26 francs to 2,453 but Roche certificates rose 65 francs to 14,650.
